Synopsis:
This is lia's main dialogue in moonrise towers. She's been taken captive (along with her brother cal) - she doesn't know if her other brother rolan is alive or dead. Lia is brave and used to being in tough situations, but she's terrified for herself anf her brother (and trying to mask it with anger). Her main dialogue occurs with her in a cell and speaking to the player on the other side of the bars. There are additional branches for when she's in one cell and the player was arrested an in the cell next to her.

Cluster Contexts:
- MOO_Jailbreak_ProdigySister.json: Lia and her brother Cal have been taken prisoner in Moonrise Towers; Lia is brave and used to danger but terrified for herself and Cal (and uncertain whether their other brother, Rolan, is alive), and she hides that fear behind anger and hostile quips. This scene is usually Lia behind bars talking to the player on the other side (with dialogue variants if the player was also arrested and ends up in the neighboring cell). Off‑screen a zealous, sadistic half‑orc Absolute jailer patrols the cells, can telepathically check for tadpoles and control who comes and goes, and the tower is on high alert after recent Execution/Audience events—any trouble may be reported or met with force. Cal is elsewhere restrained but desperate to help, and Lia may initially assume the player is a cult sympathizer (or a grove ally), so her suspicion can soften only if the player convincingly offers aid.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Sister.json: Lia has been rescued from Moonrise Towers by the player and is now in Last Light. This dialogue covers multiple states: Rolan is missing, Rolan is dead, Rolan and Lia had a fight (player must pass a persuade to calm the fight, pass and fail states here), and a general state for when cal, lia and rolan are all alive and well and Lia is grateful to the player.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Brother.json: Cal has been rescued from Moonrise Towers by the player and is now in Last Light. This dialogue covers multiple states: Rolan is missing, Rolan is dead, Rolan and Cal had a fight (player must pass a persuade to calm the fight, pass and fail states here), and a general state for when cal, lia and rolan are all alive and well and cal is grateful to the player.
- HAV_ProdigyLament_Reunion.json: Cal and/or Lia have been rescued from Moonrise towers and reunited with Rolan in Last Light Inn. It is initially a tense scene - Rolan was worried sick/is angry one of his siblings is dead and is taking it out on his family. It is up to the player to calm them down and remind them of what is important - family.
- MOO_Jailbreak_ProdigyBrother.json: Cal is a tiefling prisoner taken to Moonrise with his siblings; he’s Rolan and Lia’s brother and is determined to rescue Lia while trying to keep up a brave front for the other captives. Off‑screen he’s been ambushed and restrained (ropes, transport, or waiting by a boat) under the watch of Moonrise guards, so he’s tense, impatient, and suspicious of outsiders—especially if the player refuses to help. The area is on high alert after recent Execution/Audience events, and a sadistic half‑orc cult guard nearby can check prisoners, control movement, and will report any trouble to her superiors (like Disciple Z’rell). Rolan is not present here; he’s at the Last Light Inn, which may influence Cal’s hopes and the urgency of his pleas.

context: Lia is a captive in Moonrise Towers, speaking from a barred cell and terrified for herself and her brother Cal (who is restrained elsewhere), while uncertain whether their other brother Rolan is alive. She’s brave and used to danger but hides her fear behind anger, hostile quips, and suspicion—often assuming outsiders are cult sympathizers until convinced otherwise. Off‑screen a zealous, sadistic half‑orc jailer patrols the cells, can telepathically check for tadpoles and control movement, and the tower is on high alert after recent Execution/Audience events, so any trouble risks brutal reprisal. Some dialogue variants play if the player is recognized as a grove ally or was arrested and placed in the neighboring cell; Lia’s antagonism will soften only if the player convincingly offers help.
